docs_quotes:
From the official @nuxt/content package README.md (shipped inside @nuxt/content@3.16.1 on npm; only navigation-related text found in that file):
"Nuxt Content reads the `content/` directory in your project, parses `.md`, `.yml`, `.csv` or `.json` files and creates a powerful data layer for your application. Bonus, use Vue components in Markdown with the [MDC syntax](https://content.nuxt.com/docs/files/markdown)."

From the official @nuxt/content package README.md feature list:
"- Navigation generation"

From the official @nuxt/content package README.md:
"- [📖  Read the documentation](https://content.nuxt.com)"

From the official nuxt/starter `content` template README.md (scaffolded 2026-09-23 via `npx nuxi@latest init nuxt-content-starter -t content`):
"Look at the [Nuxt Content documentation](https://content.nuxt.com) to learn more."

Inclusion: the docs' stated criteria for what makes a page appear in the navigation tree (unverified).

Hiding: whether the docs document a hide flag (e.g. `navigation: false`), its exact field name, accepted values (boolean false vs string "false"), and where it may be set (page frontmatter vs directory config) (unverified).
Ordering primary key: whether the docs name an ordering key (e.g. stem/filename order, numeric filename prefixes, `navigation.order`, `_dir.yml`/`navigation.yml` position) (unverified).
Tie-break: what the docs say when two items share the same order value, or when no order is given (unverified).
Default order: what the docs say the order is when no ordering key is present (unverified).
Direction: whether the docs specify ascending vs descending (unverified).
Grouping: how the docs say sections are formed (per-directory config files; the v2 `_dir.yml` vs v3 `.navigation.yml` naming) and the rule for section ordering (unverified).

API surface: whether the docs present `queryCollectionNavigation()` / `useContentNavigation()` (v2) as the navigation API and which major version each belongs to (unverified from docs; the installed v3.16.1 runtime exposes `queryCollectionNavigation`).
